1#main: The law of hanging an omission and the law of one who errs in writing the Name. In it are 13 seifim. If he erred and skipped a word or more, he may hang it between the lines, but not in the space between page and page.
2#main: Even though he says at the beginning of the book that he writes it for the sake of the sanctity of a Sefer Torah, each time he writes one of the Names that are not erased, he must say that he writes for the sake of the sanctity of the Name; and if he did not do so, it is invalid (so it appears from the Rosh, and likewise Semag and Sefer HaTerumah). {Rama: If he wrote names of other gods for the sake of sanctity, it is not invalid, for it is like one who dedicates blemished animals to the altar, which are not holy (Beit Yosef in the name of Rashbatz).}
3#main: When writing the Name—even the king of Israel who asks after his welfare—one does not answer him; and if he was writing two Names one after another, it is permitted to interrupt between them; and when he returns to write the second Name he must again say that he writes it for the sake of the sanctity of the Name.
4#main: When he dips the quill to write the Name, he should not begin immediately with the Name to write, lest excess ink be upon it and the writing not come out straight; rather he should intend to leave one letter from what he writes before the Name, and with that letter he should begin to write. (And if he did not do so, he should seek a letter that needs ink, fill it, and write the Name) (Beit Yosef in the name of Mordechai).
5#main: If he wrote the divine Names in ink and threw gold upon them—it is invalid.
6#main: If he forgot to write the entire Name, he hangs it between the lines; but part of the Name on the line and part hanging is invalid.
7#main: It is permitted to write the Name on the place of erasure and on the place of scraping. (And there is no difference in this between a Sefer Torah and other books) (so too in Sefer HaTerumah).
8#main: All letters of the Name must be within the page, and none of them may extend at all outside the page.
9#main: It is forbidden to erase even one letter of the seven Names that are not erased, nor from the letters attached after them, such as the final kaf of "elohecha" and the final mem of "eloheichem." And these are the seven Names: the Tetragrammaton; the Name Adnut; El; Eloah; Elohim; Shaddai; Tzevaot. And some also read Ehyeh—"Asher Ehyeh" (Tur).
10#main: If he wrote "El" from "Elohim," "Yah" from the Name—it is not erased; but "Shad" from Shaddai and "Tzev" from Tzevaot are erased. {Rama: And likewise "Ad" from Adnut, or "Eh" from Ehyeh (Yerushalmi, first chapter of Megillah). And some are stringent in this (Tosafot, chapter Shevuat Ha'eidut, in the name of R' Chananel). And the Name that they write in siddurim with two yuds and one on top of them—it is permitted to erase if for a need (Piskei Maharai siman 148).}
11#main: If a letter stuck to its fellow in the letters of the Name, he may scrape it. {Rama: Ink that spilled on the Name—it is permitted to erase it in order to correct it, for this is not a manner of erasure but of correction (Beit Yosef in the name of Maseches Soferim and Hagahos Maimoniyos chapter 6). If the hei of the Name bent so its leg touches the roof—if it truly touches until it appears like a chet, it is permitted to erase or scrape the leg and correct it; but if it touches only slightly, there is doubt whether it is permitted (Beit Yosef in the name of R' Yitzchak Alexandri).}
12#main: One who wrote "Yehudah" and did not put in it the dalet—he hangs the dalet above; had he been writing the Name and wrote "Yehudah," he makes a hei from the dalet and erases the final hei.
13#main: A vessel on which a Name was written—one cuts out the place of the Name and buries it. {Rama: And it is forbidden to write the Name l'chatchila except in a book, lest it come to disgrace; therefore they are careful not to write the Name in a letter. And some are careful even with the word "shalom" not to finish writing it (Maharil in the name of Tashbetz).}
